script.opening_words: What if I told you that despite working harder than any generation before them, millennials and Gen Z have somehow managed to become the poorest young adults in modern history. Not because they're lazy or spending all their money on avocado toast, but because the economic game has been rigged against them from day one. My name is Nick and today we're diving deep into why an entire generation is getting financially destroyed and it has absolutely nothing to do
script.ending_words: they're trying to play a game where someone changed all the rules without telling them. Housing costs have exploded. Education has become a luxury item and basic transportation now requires a small loan. The American dream didn't die, it just became prohibitively expensive. If you found this eye openening, make sure to subscribe and let me know in the comments what generational financial myth you'd like me to tackle next.
script.analysis: Full 19564 canonical characters read. A grievance essay: generational hook; 86% purchasing-power claim; housing price-to-income 1988 vs 2022, bubble and UK comparisons; homes vs CPI since 1990; demand factors (population, marriage, Pew living arrangements); student debt and tuition; credential inflation and starting salaries; car payments, gas and insurance; credit cards; latte objection; social media; gig economy; retirement (Social Security, pensions); healthcare; childcare and child cost; mental health; systemic-change argument; tech concentration; international comparison; practical tips (rent share, 3-5% down, avoid car payments); close. Directly verified (FRED): 1988 $110,000 and 2022 $433,000 median home prices; stated incomes wrong ($27,230 and $74,580), so the 1988 ratio is right but 2022 is 5.8, not over 6. CPI multiplier is 2.48x, not 2.31x. Unsupported: 86% purchasing-power loss; healthcare tripled. The stored ending is complete; heavy filler words.
beat_map: Hook: poorest young adults; not avocado toast.
Bubble and UK comparison; long-run trend.
Tips: rent share, down payments, cars.
